title: Variables 1
code:
count = 44;
half_count = count // 2
print(count, half_count)
count = 99
print(count, half_count)    
half_count = count / 2
print(count, half_count)
count = count + 100
print(count, half_count)
count = "100"
half_count = "count"
print(count, half_count)

lines.explanation: Dividing the value of 'count' by two and asigning the resultant value to the variable 'half_count'
Printing the value of both 'count' and 'half_count'. The result at this point will be '44 22'
This statement re-assigns (assigns again) new value to the variable 'count'. Note the new value of the variable 'count' is '99'
Printing the value of both 'count and 'half_count'. At this point the value of 'half_count' is still 22. Hence this statement will print out '99 22'
Now since the new value of the variable 'count' is '99', the variable 'half_count' will get the value '49.5'
Printing out the new value of 'count' and 'half_count'
This statement adds '100' to the current value of 'count' and assigns the sum back to the variable 'count'. In shour it updates the value of the 'count'
Now the value of 'count' and 'half_count' will be '199' and '49.5'
This statement assigns a string '100' to the variable 'count'. Do note that the "100" is enclosed in the double quotes. Hence, it is not an integer value but a string.
This is again a tricky statement. Here a string 'count' is assigned to the variable 'half_count'. The value of 'half_count' will be updated with a string 'count' after this statement
Printing the new value of 'count' and 'half_count'
